findings.highlight: I land without hurting myself.
findings.evidenceJa: 着地時に足首をひねる事もなく、行動はイメージどおり行えた。
findings.governingReading: Shirou lands without twisting an ankle and executes the entire action exactly as imaged.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only lack of injury and omits that his movement matches his mental image, a recurring link between his physical precision, archery, and magecraft.

findings.highlight: It feels like a giant blob of jelly fell on top of me…
findings.evidenceJa: 脳天から、どぶ、と巨大なゼリーが、落ちてきた、ような。
findings.governingReading: It feels as if a huge mass of jelly fell with a heavy splat directly onto the crown of his head.
findings.explanation: “On top of me” removes the exact head impact and どぶ’s viscous heavy sensation, weakening the bodily metaphor for Gandr’s onset.

findings.highlight: The Gandr Shot, a magic that’ll infect the target with a cold
findings.evidenceJa: 狙った者に病を与えるというガンド撃ち
findings.governingReading: Gandr is a curse-shot said to inflict illness upon its chosen target.
findings.explanation: The English narrows 病 to a common cold and recasts supernatural infliction as infectious transmission, materially changing Gandr’s curse mechanism and possible severity.

findings.highlight: my body is so sick
findings.evidenceJa: 重い熱病にかかってしまった
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s body has been struck by a severe febrile illness that leaves him unable to move himself.
findings.explanation: “So sick” deletes fever and the explicit disease category, reducing the curse’s bodily effect to generic sickness.

findings.highlight: I hear Tohsaka’s voice from afar, as if she’s contacting me from the moon.
findings.evidenceJa: まるで月あたりから交信しているような頼りなさで、遠坂の声がする。
findings.governingReading: Rin’s voice reaches him with the faint, unreliable quality of a transmission from somewhere around the moon.
findings.explanation: The English preserves distance and the lunar comparison but omits 頼りなさ, the failing, tenuous quality of Shirou’s perception as consciousness collapses.

findings.highlight: My consciousness shuts down as if it’s shorted out.
findings.evidenceJa: バチン、と。ショートしたように意識が落ちた。
findings.governingReading: With an electrical snap, his consciousness drops as though a circuit has shorted.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the short-circuit simile but omits バチン, the sharp sensory instant that joins Rin’s touch to the blackout.

findings.highlight: I rouse my sleepy mind and pull myself up.
findings.evidenceJa: ぼんやりとした意識を起こして、二度寝したがる根性に活を入れる。
findings.governingReading: Shirou rouses his hazy consciousness and gives a bracing mental kick to the part of him that wants to fall back asleep.
findings.explanation: “Pull myself up” generalizes the action and omits both the specific urge to sleep again and his forceful self-rebuke.

findings.highlight: I should be preparing breakfast now.
findings.evidenceJa: とっくに朝食の準備をしなくてはならない時間だ。
findings.governingReading: It is already well past the time when Shirou must begin breakfast preparations.
findings.explanation: The English removes とっくに and makes the duty merely current, weakening the abnormal lateness that the erased-memory scene depends on.

findings.highlight: I’ll make dinner, so please forgive me.
findings.evidenceJa: なんか凄く眠くて起きられなくてさ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou explains that he was extraordinarily sleepy and physically could not wake.
findings.explanation: The English omits the entire explanation, making this look like ordinary oversleeping rather than an unexplained aftereffect of Rin’s attack and memory alteration.

findings.highlight: so please let me.
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩は大人しくしててください
findings.governingReading: Sakura tells Shirou to behave himself and stay out of the cooking because tonight is her turn.
findings.explanation: “Please let me” changes the commanded actor from Shirou to Sakura and removes her gently forceful instruction that he remain still, shifting their domestic agency.

findings.highlight: I want to make it up to you for sleeping in.
findings.evidenceJa: 寝坊の汚名を返上したいんだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou wants to wipe away the disgrace or bad name of having overslept.
findings.explanation: The English turns restoration of his own competence and reputation into repayment owed personally to Sakura, changing the motivation of his insistence.

findings.highlight: I leave the house as well.
findings.evidenceJa: いつも通り、悠々と家を後にする。
findings.governingReading: Thirty minutes after Taiga and Sakura, Shirou leaves the house with his usual unhurried ease.
findings.explanation: The English omits 悠々 and replaces habitual manner with merely “as well,” flattening the false-normal atmosphere.

findings.highlight: I breathe in the perfect morning air.
findings.evidenceJa: 何一つ欠けていない朝の空気を肺に取り込む。
findings.governingReading: Shirou fills his lungs with morning air from which not a single thing seems absent.
findings.explanation: “Perfect” evaluates pleasant quality; the source insists on completeness, an ironic motif because a person has been erased from his awareness.

findings.highlight: I notice that a female student is looking at me.
findings.evidenceJa: なんとなく、通り過ぎる女生徒と目が合った。
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s eyes happen to meet those of a passing female student.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the girl a prior one-sided gaze and Shirou merely notices it, changing mutual accidental eye contact into her watching him.

findings.highlight: Were you glaring at Tohsaka?
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂とにらみ合っていたのか？
findings.governingReading: Issei asks whether Shirou and Tohsaka were glaring at each other.
findings.explanation: The English makes Shirou the sole aggressor and Rin the object, removing the reciprocal confrontation Issei thinks he witnessed.

findings.highlight: Buddhist scriptures
findings.evidenceJa: 南無観世音菩薩
findings.governingReading: Issei voices the specific invocation “Namu Kanzeon Bosatsu,” calling on the bodhisattva of compassion.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a recognizable mock-prayer for Shirou’s fate with generic scriptures, erasing the joke’s exact religious form and Issei’s temple upbringing.

findings.highlight: I watch him go as I stand there.
findings.evidenceJa: その後ろ姿を見送って、ぼんやりと立ち尽くした。
findings.governingReading: Shirou watches Issei’s receding back and remains rooted in place, blank and dazed.
findings.explanation: The English omits ぼんやり and 立ち尽くす’s inability to move, weakening the first bodily sign that the supposedly normal morning is wrong.

findings.highlight: I feel uneasy for some reason
findings.evidenceJa: カタチのない焦燥に包まれて
findings.governingReading: Shirou is enveloped by a formless agitation or urgent anxiety he cannot identify.
findings.explanation: “Uneasy for some reason” weakens焦燥’s restless urgency and removes the image of being surrounded by an anxiety with no shape, central to erased memory pressing without content.

findings.highlight: It’s about a meter and a half down. I can easily take this kind of height…!
findings.evidenceJa: 階段の踊り場まで一メートル半、その程度の高さなら難なく着地できる……！
findings.governingReading: The staircase landing is one and a half metres below, a height Shirou can land without difficulty.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the drop but omits the landing he has selected, making his calculated escape geometry abstract.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka’s magic.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の魔術。
findings.governingReading: Shirou identifies the effect as Rin’s magecraft.
findings.explanation: “Magic” collapses 魔術 into the setting’s distinct higher category instead of preserving the technical term being explained through Gandr.

findings.highlight: Hmm. Then let’s cook together.
findings.evidenceJa: うーん、そうですね。じゃあ夕飯は半分コという事で。
findings.governingReading: Sakura proposes splitting the dinner work or responsibility half and half.
findings.explanation: “Let’s cook together” removes the explicit equal division and substitutes simultaneous joint cooking for Sakura’s negotiated domestic compromise.

findings.highlight: As the school gate closes, I feel like I’m locked out from something.
findings.evidenceJa: 学校の門が閉まるように、何かに締め出されたような気がする。
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels shut out by something, as though a school gate were closing.
findings.explanation: The English turns the closing gate from a simile for abstract exclusion into an event occurring in the scene, weakening the memory-related ambiguity.

findings.highlight: I
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は、たしか
findings.governingReading: Shirou begins “I, if I remember correctly…” but cannot complete the attempt to recover the thought.
findings.explanation: The English retains only the pronoun and omits たしか, removing the explicit uncertainty that marks his failed reach for an erased memory.
